encounters.cc: Bilateral eye discharge and conjunctival redness noted 9 days after birth with recent respiratory symptoms

lines: Bilateral eye discharge and conjunctival redness noted 9 days after birth with recent respiratory symptoms
The child was born at 38 weeks gestation via vaginal delivery to a 23-year-old mother who had limited prenatal care.
The mother reports that her baby began developing mild conjunctival redness and watery eye discharge in both eyes about 9 days ago.
Over the past two days, the discharge has become mucopurulent, and his eyelids appear mildly swollen.
She also notes that her infant has been breathing more rapidly, with audible crackles when crying, and has had decreased feeding and increased fussiness.
The infant received erythromycin ointment at birth.
- History of necrotizing enterocolitis (medically managed, resolved)
- Feeding difficulties requiring nasogastric tube supplementation
- Prematurity (born 38 weeks gestation with late preterm complications)
He is otherwise up to date on postnatal care.
- Ferrous sulfate 2 mg/kg elemental iron PO daily
There is no known family history of atopy or genetic illness.
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: N/A (pediatric patient).
Vital signs reveal a temperature of 38.1°C (100.6°F), respiratory rate of 60/min, and pulse of 160/min.
Lung auscultation reveals diffuse bilateral crackles without wheezes or rhonchi.
An image of the patient's eyes is shown below.

encounters.cc: 1-day history of poor feeding, vomiting, and abdominal distension in a 3-week-old

lines: 1-day history of poor feeding, vomiting, and abdominal distension in a 3-week-old
The 3-week-old with uncorrected cyanotic congenital heart disease and chronic gastric outlet obstruction presents following recent chlamydial conjunctivitis.
The mother reports the infant has been feeding poorly, vomited twice since yesterday, and his abdomen appears swollen.
- History of necrotizing enterocolitis (medically managed, resolved)
- Feeding difficulties requiring nasogastric tube supplementation
- Prematurity (born 38 weeks gestation with late preterm complications)
The infant's medical history is significant for prematurity and a patent ductus arteriosus, which is being managed medically.
- Ferrous sulfate 2 mg/kg elemental iron PO daily
- Mother with Chlamydia trachomatis infection (perinatal, age 23 at delivery)
- Maternal history of limited prenatal care
- No known family history of congenital heart disease
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: N/A (pediatric patient).
On examination, the infant is afebrile, with a heart rate of 160 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 60 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation of 92% on room air
His abdomen is distended and tender to palpation, with visible bowel loops.
There is no guarding or rebound tenderness.
A blood gas analysis shows metabolic acidosis.
An abdominal x-ray reveals pneumatosis intestinalis.

encounters.cc: Episodes of apnea and lethargy requiring respiratory support during NEC treatment

lines: Episodes of apnea and lethargy requiring respiratory support during NEC treatment
The patient is a late preterm neonate with cyanotic congenital heart disease returning following emergency department evaluation for necrotizing enterocolitis.

The infant is brought to the emergency department by concerned parents due to episodes of apnea and lethargy and has been exclusively fed with expressed breast milk via a nasogastric tube since birth.
- History of necrotizing enterocolitis (medically managed, resolved)
- Feeding difficulties requiring nasogastric tube supplementation
- Prematurity (born 38 weeks gestation with late preterm complications)
- Ferrous sulfate 2 mg/kg elemental iron PO daily
- Mother with Chlamydia trachomatis infection (perinatal, age 23 at delivery)
- Maternal history of limited prenatal care
- No known family history of congenital heart disease
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: N/A (pediatric patient).
His vital signs are as follows: temperature 37.2°C, heart rate 160 beats per minute, respiratory rate 50 breaths per minute, and oxygen saturation 92% on room air.
On examination, the infant appears lethargic with a distended abdomen and decreased bowel sounds.
An abdominal x-ray is obtained, which shows pneumatosis intestinalis.

encounters.cc: Recurrent episodes of bilious vomiting over the past week with acute abdominal distension

lines: Recurrent episodes of bilious vomiting over the past week with acute abdominal distension

The infant with uncorrected cyanotic congenital heart disease, hemodynamically significant patent ductus arteriosus, and history of intestinal malrotation status post repair returns one month after necrotizing enterocolitis treatment with recurrent symptoms.
The infant was born at term via normal vaginal delivery with an uncomplicated prenatal course.
The mother reports that the infant has been increasingly fussy and has had difficulty with feeding, often vomiting shortly after breastfeeding.
The vomiting has progressively become more forceful and is now greenish in color.
The infant has had fewer wet diapers and has not passed stool in the last 24 hours.
- History of necrotizing enterocolitis (medically managed, resolved)
- Feeding difficulties requiring nasogastric tube supplementation
- Prematurity (born 38 weeks gestation with late preterm complications)
- Ferrous sulfate 2 mg/kg elemental iron PO daily
- Mother with Chlamydia trachomatis infection (perinatal, age 23 at delivery)
- Maternal history of limited prenatal care
- No known family history of congenital heart disease
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: N/A (pediatric patient).
On examination, the infant appears lethargic and has a distended abdomen with visible peristaltic waves.
Bowel sounds are high-pitched and hyperactive.
Rectal examination reveals an empty rectal vault.
An abdominal x-ray shows a "double bubble" sign without distal gas.

lines: Persistent, forceful, non-bilious vomiting after feeding for the past week

The patient is a male infant with uncorrected cyanotic congenital heart disease, hemodynamically significant patent ductus arteriosus, and a history of intestinal malrotation status post surgical repair who presents with persistent feeding difficulties.
He exhibits forceful, non-bloody, non-bilious vomiting after feeding for the past week.
- History of necrotizing enterocolitis (medically managed, resolved)
- Feeding difficulties requiring nasogastric tube supplementation
- Prematurity (born 38 weeks gestation with late preterm complications)
- Ferrous sulfate 2 mg/kg elemental iron PO daily
- Mother with Chlamydia trachomatis infection (perinatal, age 23 at delivery)
- Maternal history of limited prenatal care

On physical examination, the infant appears dehydrated, and a small, firm, olive-shaped mass is palpated in the right upper abdomen.
Laboratory studies are obtained to evaluate for electrolyte abnormalities.

encounters.cc: Repeated episodes of bilious vomiting over the past 6 hours and no bowel movement for 24 hours

lines: Repeated episodes of bilious vomiting over the past 6 hours and no bowel movement for 24 hours
Patient with cyanotic congenital heart disease and intestinal malrotation repair presents.
The parents report that the infant has been increasingly fussy and has not had a bowel movement in 24 hours.
- Gastric outlet obstruction or Peptic ulcer disease (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
- History of necrotizing enterocolitis (medically managed, resolved)
- Feeding difficulties requiring nasogastric tube supplementation
- Prematurity (born 38 weeks gestation with late preterm complications)
The infant was born at term via normal spontaneous vaginal delivery without complications.
- Ferrous sulfate 2 mg/kg elemental iron PO daily
- Mother with Chlamydia trachomatis infection (perinatal, age 23 at delivery)
- Maternal history of limited prenatal care
- No known family history of congenital heart disease
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: N/A (pediatric patient).
Vital signs show a heart rate of 180 beats per minute, respiratory rate of 60 breaths per minute, blood pressure of 70/40 mmHg, and temperature of 37.6°C (99.7°F).
On examination, the infant appears lethargic and has a distended abdomen that is tender to palpation.
There is no guarding or rebound tenderness.
Rectal examination reveals an empty rectal vault.
An abdominal x-ray reveals multiple air-fluid levels and a paucity of gas in the distal bowel.

encounters.cc: 3-day history of cough and difficulty breathing with low-grade fever during winter months

lines: 3-day history of cough and difficulty breathing with low-grade fever during winter months

The patient is a 1-year-old male with uncorrected cyanotic congenital heart disease, hemodynamically significant patent ductus arteriosus, status post surgical repair of intestinal malrotation, and chronic gastric outlet obstruction who is brought to the emergency department by his parents in the middle of winter due to a 3-day history of cough and difficulty breathing.
His parents report that he has had a runny nose and low-grade fever for the past 5 days.
The cough has progressively worsened, and today they noticed that he is breathing faster and his chest seems to be "sucking in" with each breath.
- Gastric outlet obstruction or Peptic ulcer disease (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
- History of necrotizing enterocolitis (medically managed, resolved)
- Feeding difficulties requiring nasogastric tube supplementation
- Prematurity (born 38 weeks gestation with late preterm complications)
He is up-to-date with his immunizations.
- Ferrous sulfate 2 mg/kg elemental iron PO daily
- Mother with Chlamydia trachomatis infection (perinatal, age 23 at delivery)
- Maternal history of limited prenatal care
- No known family history of congenital heart disease
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: N/A (pediatric patient).
Oxygen saturation on room air is 92%.
On examination, the child is tachypneic with a respiratory rate of 60 breaths per minute, and intercostal and subcostal retractions are noted.
Auscultation of the chest reveals diffuse wheezes and crackles bilaterally.
The rest of the examination is unremarkable.
A chest x-ray is performed and shows peribronchial cuffing and increased interstitial markings without focal consolidation.

encounters.cc: Irritability, feeding refusal, tachypnea, and intermittent cyanosis requiring cardiology evaluation and care planning

lines: Irritability, feeding refusal, tachypnea, and intermittent cyanosis requiring cardiology evaluation and care planning

The patient is a 3-year-old male with uncorrected cyanotic congenital heart disease, hemodynamically significant patent ductus arteriosus, chronic gastric outlet obstruction, and feeding difficulties requiring nasogastric tube supplementation who presents for cardiology follow-up.
His mother reports that he has been irritable for the past 2 days and has refused to feed since this morning.
She also noticed that he has been breathing rapidly and his lips occasionally turn blue, especially during feeding.
- Gastric outlet obstruction or Peptic ulcer disease (diagnosed 2020-04-15)
- History of necrotizing enterocolitis (medically managed, resolved)
- Feeding difficulties requiring nasogastric tube supplementation
- Prematurity (born 38 weeks gestation with late preterm complications)
The patient's past medical history is significant for a murmur identified at birth, but no follow-up was done.
- Ferrous sulfate 2 mg/kg elemental iron PO daily
- Mother with Chlamydia trachomatis infection (perinatal, age 23 at delivery)
- Maternal history of limited prenatal care
- No known family history of congenital heart disease
Smoking: Never. Alcohol: Never. Occupation: N/A (pediatric patient).
Respiratory rate 70 breaths per minute, heart rate 160 beats per minute, oxygen saturation 88% on room air
On examination, the infant is tachypneic.
A systolic murmur is heard at the left sternal border.
Arterial blood gas: pH 7.32, PaCO2 30 mmHg, PaO2 60 mmHg, HCO3- 18 mEq/L
Chest X-ray shows an enlarged cardiac silhouette and increased pulmonary vascular markings.
